title: Ernest 44, carrying instruments and brother Tellis Washington's orchestra
summary: Welch learned 44 from Ernest 44, played country suppers, then joined his trombonist brother Tellis Washington's orchestra.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: And another guy by the name of Ernest 44. Now, he learned me how to play a record he called 44 on a guitar. And I learned that piece, and I've been playing it ever since. That record has made me right amount of money since I've been playing it.
Who cut the record? Do you remember who made it?
No, the boy called Ernest 44. That's his name.
And he made the record himself. Yes, sir. And you knew him personally.
Yes, sir. I knew him personally.

And so I'd just run around from one to another and one from another. Those guys would go to plays to play music. I'd ask the one to let me carry his instrument for him. I'd go to the dance with him, carry his instrument. When they stopped for intermission, I'd grab one of them and go to play in it. Yeah. So finally, I got good enough for the make a couple of songs of my own. And then I'd start playing for country suppers myself, getting $3 and $4 an hour for playing at those suppers. Well, I did pretty good. I made, taking care of my wife and three kids and a water bill and a house rent and grocery bill for three years doing that myself. Well, after I learned pretty good, my brother had an orchestra in Memphis, Tennessee. Well, they broke up and they come up in Mississippi. And he asked me would I join them. So he learned me a lot. He was a trombone player. So he learned me a lot.
His name was Tellis Washington. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
